title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Null Result on a Deterministic Synthetic Task Pool
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measured the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic verifier+repair step (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and a deterministic validator we selected K=200 tasks via a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule. A single shared generator output per task (shared_initial_generation) was evaluated in both arms. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair pathway was never invoked. The null is a ceiling case for this specific task/model/validator regime; we release full execution and scoring artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), validator traces, and analysis logs to enable replay and to inform future evaluations that sample failure‑rich distributions.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation can increase operational velocity but also risks introducing regressions (reachability loss, service disruption). A common architectural mitigation is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes configuration commands, a deterministic verifier detects safety violations, and an automated repair step attempts to correct violations before apply. Prior work advocates this pipeline but provides limited preregistered causal estimates of the verifier’s marginal effect under controlled task sampling.

Research question. Under a preregistered paired design, does inserting a deterministic verifier+repair step reduce the rate of regression‑causing configuration changes compared with accepting an LLM candidate directly (paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)?

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory run (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with deterministic task selection and auditorily archived artifacts; (2) a reproducible execution manifest and scoring trace release enabling exact replay (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...); (3) an artifact‑grounded report of a ceiling/null outcome (paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p=1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]) and operational guidance for designing future verifier utility evaluations.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans LLM‑assisted configuration generation, verifier‑augmented pipelines, and formal verification of network configurations. Benchmarks and pipelines (e.g., Cornetto and recent generate–validate–repair proposals) emphasize formal checks and iterative repair to avoid regressions. Other studies argue for translation‑only AI plus solver‑based reasoning. Our study contributes a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired estimate that isolates the verifier’s marginal effect under a fixed generator output per task and deterministic validator.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The experiment was preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256: a6d73a5c...) and specified the paired estimand, deterministic sampling, validator semantics, and analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar (paired binary) with paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) for 95% CI.

Task sampling and shared initial generation. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and filtered to those covered by the preregistered validator. To avoid human selection bias we sorted task intents by SHA‑256(intent_string) and selected the first K=200 unique tasks (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 f1d447b7...). For each task we performed a single generator call (shared_initial_generation) whose output candidate_c was supplied to both arms: baseline accepts candidate_c; guarded first validates candidate_c with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and may invoke at most one repair call if violations occur (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). This fixed‑generator shared design isolates the verifier’s marginal effect by holding generator variability constant but prevents generator adaptation to validator feedback; as a result repairs can only be triggered if the initial candidate fails validation.

Model, provider auditing, and artifacts. Requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: 1acce9255...). Execution and provider call traces were archived (execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/responses/*.txt) and per‑call hashes recorded to detect caching or cross‑condition reuse; no cross‑condition cache reuse was observed (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Raw results and per‑task scoring traces are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...).

Validator and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses candidate text into structured field changes and enforces workflow invariants (protected interfaces, must_be_down_for_fields, group minimum‑up constraints). The confirmatory outcome was validator.valid (binary). Scorer outputs include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, final_state snapshot, and violation codes; representative scoring JSONs are in execution/scoring/ with SHA‑256s recorded in the manifest.

Statistical reasoning for the degenerate outcome. When no discordant pairs exist (n10 = n01 = 0), the paired estimate is exactly zero and the exact McNemar two‑sided p equals 1.00 (all observed pairs concordant). A paired bootstrap over the empirical paired outcomes will also produce a degenerate percentile CI [0.00,0.00] when every bootstrap draw has identical paired counts; we used 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The preregistered power calculation assumed a nontrivial baseline failure rate (~0.20); because the observed baseline failure rate was 0.0 the original power assumption did not apply — we therefore report exact paired inference and bootstrap CIs as the appropriate description of uncertainty for this observed ceiling case.

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Representative per‑task scoring traces are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 3055f874...).

Repair and repair_invocation accounting. The guarded repair path was never invoked: repair_applied=false for every guarded episode in execution/scoring/*.json (see representative traces). Consequently no additional model calls beyond the shared initial generation were used by guarded.

Task difficulty summary (artifact‑grounded sample and availability note). Representative_tasks entries archived in the bundle include explicit difficulty metadata for sample tasks. Among the six representative tasks shown in the archived manifest, difficulty levels are: medium=1, hard=2, very_hard=3. A full aggregated difficulty histogram across all K=200 tasks was not produced by the archived analysis artifacts; per‑task difficulty metadata is present in execution/scoring/*.json and can be deterministically aggregated by replaying the scoring JSONs (paths and SHA‑256s are archived).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The run produced a reproducible ceiling/null outcome: under the selected deterministic task pool, requested_model, and deterministic validator every shared generator candidate satisfied the validation constraints and no repairs were applied. This is a valid empirical outcome of the preregistered experiment: the verifier had no marginal effect because there were no failing initial candidates to correct.

Why the ceiling arose (artifact‑grounded). Three artifact‑grounded factors explain the result: (1) task selection required validator coverage, biasing the sample toward intents the validator already covers; (2) the requested_model (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that respected the explicit workflow constraints encoded in the task payloads; (3) the shared_initial_generation paired design fixes the generator output across arms and prevents generator adaptation to validator feedback — repairs can only occur if the initial candidate fails validation. All relevant artifacts and logs (task_manifest.jsonl, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/provider_calls/*.json) are archived for audit.

Design implications. To detect verifier/repair utility with a confirmatory paired estimate, future runs should (artifact‑grounded advice): (A) sample or construct task banks with intentionally failure‑rich or boundary cases (historical misconfigurations); (B) include multiple generator strengths (including weaker models) to produce a nontrivial baseline failure rate; (C) consider interactive generator–verifier workflows (which change the estimand) if the objective is to measure end‑to‑end closed‑loop improvement; (D) always publish per‑task validator coverage and difficulty aggregates (these can be computed from execution/scoring/*.json and are archived here for replay).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired design and deterministic synthetic task pool, the verifier produced no marginal change: H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes) was not supported — both arms yielded 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; paired difference = 0.00; p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. This outcome represents a ceiling/null case for the chosen task/model/validator regime and does not generalize to failure‑rich production distributions. We release full artifacts (preregistration, raw responses, provider traces, scoring JSONs, execution manifest, analysis logs) to enable exact replay and to support the design of future, failure‑rich evaluations that can demonstrate verifier and repair value where baseline generator errors are present.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without further experiments.
Synthetic deterministic task pool and deterministic sampling — external validity to production intents, vendor diversity, and noisy telemetry is limited.
Primary outcome depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; construct validity is tied to validator coverage of real regression modes.
Ceiling effect: observed baseline success = 100% eliminated ability to demonstrate verifier/repair benefit under this design and task sample.

Aggregated difficulty histogram across K=200 tasks was not produced in the archived analysis; per‑task difficulty metadata exists in execution/scoring/*.json and can be deterministically aggregated by replaying those artifacts.
